real_world.product: Whitbread Engine, Boulton and Watt rotative beam engine of 1785
real_world.use: Watt's parallel motion with its copying links guides the piston rod straight from the rocking beam; preserved at the Powerhouse Museum, Sydney.
real_world.note: The beam plus parallel-motion links form the Watt-type chain listed for this mechanism; the source names it parallel motion, not a six-bar.

real_world.product: Model Boulton and Watt condensing beam engine, c. 1800 (object 1869-64)
real_world.maker: Boulton and Watt (model); Science Museum Group
real_world.use: Working scale model of a double-acting beam engine showing the parallel motion linkage on the beam.

real_world.product: Yeti 160E electric enduro mountain bike (Sixfinity suspension)
real_world.use: A six-bar rear suspension sets anti-squat, leverage ratio and progression of the rear wheel path.
real_world.note: Source says six-bar; the Stephenson classification is inferred from the published link layout (two ternary bodies not sharing a joint).

real_world.product: Level One Engineering bicycle rear suspension system (US10160512B2)
real_world.use: Patented bicycle rear suspension built on a Stephenson III (and Stephenson II) six-bar to tune the axle path.
real_world.note: Patent, not a named retail product.

real_world.product: Mondo Spider ride-on walking machine
real_world.use: Its eight steel legs are Klann linkages, a Stephenson III six-bar, driven from a common crank.

real_world.product: MELFA RP series compact assembly robots (RP-1AH to RP-5AH)
real_world.use: A closed five-link arm driven by two base motors places small parts with high positioning accuracy.

real_world.product: Line-us internet-connected drawing robot
real_world.use: A small motor-driven arm moves a pen across paper to copy what the user draws on screen.
real_world.note: The fetched article confirms the product but does not describe the arm as a five-bar.

real_world.product: Mondo Spider ride-on walking machine
real_world.use: Eight Klann-linkage legs carry a rider; originally hydraulic-driven by a Honda V-twin, later electric.

real_world.product: Mondo Spider (eatART) machine profile
real_world.use: Describes the full-size eight-legged electro-mechanical walker as built and run by its Vancouver team.
real_world.note: Same machine as above; the page does not name the linkage.

real_world.product: Joe Klann walking device patent US6364040
real_world.use: The original patent for the single-crank walking leg whose foot moves straight on the ground then lifts and steps.
real_world.note: Patent rather than product; real Klann-leg products are scarce beyond the Mondo Spider.

real_world.product: Theo Jansen Strandbeests (Animaris Rigide Properans, Animaris Mulus and others) exhibition
real_world.maker: Theo Jansen; Contemporary Art Museum Kumamoto
real_world.use: Full-size wind-powered beach animals walk on crank-driven Jansen legs.

real_world.product: Animaris Ordis Strandbeests at MIT Media Lab
real_world.use: Real Strandbeests walked on their leg linkages and crankshaft; Jansen explained the leg mechanism.

real_world.product: Strandbeests (Animaris Suspendisse and others)
real_world.use: Sails drive a central crankshaft that moves an array of rotating legs.

real_world.product: Parolin Racing Kart adjustable steering column support
real_world.use: A slide moves the steering column mount to change the kart's Ackermann angle in seconds.

real_world.product: L'Obeissante steam omnibus, 1873
real_world.maker: Amedee Bollee; Musee des arts et metiers, Paris
real_world.use: Early road vehicle with double-pivot steering of the front wheels, an early working application of Ackermann-type geometry.
real_world.note: Page notes its smooth steering but does not detail the geometry.

real_world.product: Kontax Nano Rhombic Stirling engine
real_world.use: Four short rods and two drive rods form a rhombus with two meshing gears to phase the displacer and piston of a beta Stirling engine.

real_world.product: Lanchester 10 hp car engine, c. 1900
real_world.use: Each piston drives two contra-rotating crankshafts through connecting rods, giving perfect balance and no side thrust.
real_world.note: Article describes the twin-crankshaft rod arrangement but does not use the word rhombic.

real_world.product: 1901 Lanchester 10/12 HP Tonneau (FRW 766)
real_world.use: Surviving car with the balanced flat-twin Lanchester engine of the rhombic-drive era.
real_world.note: Page confirms the car and flat-twin engine but not the crank arrangement.

real_world.product: Vauxhall/Opel Astra (sixth generation, Astra J) rear suspension
real_world.use: A Watt's linkage on the torsion beam locates the axle sideways so softer bushes can be used.

real_world.product: Chevrolet Cruze rear suspension
real_world.use: Two equal horizontal links on each side form a Watt's linkage that locates the rear beam laterally.

real_world.product: Whiteline Watts linkage KDT916 for 2005-on Ford Mustang
real_world.use: Bolt-on kit that centres the 8.8 live rear axle with a Watt's link in place of a Panhard rod.

real_world.product: Yeti Cycles six-bar rear suspension (US 2020/0247500)
real_world.use: A Chebyshev four-bar guides the swingarm's lower pivot along a nearly straight path.

real_world.product: Steam engine at the 1873 Vienna Exhibition
real_world.maker: P. L. Chebyshev (reported in Ferguson, Kinematics of Mechanisms from the Time of Watt)
real_world.use: Chebyshev's straight-line mechanism, combined with an Evans linkage, guided the engine's piston rod.

real_world.product: Chebyshev plantigrade (walking) machine, 1878
real_world.maker: P. L. Chebyshev; Polytechnic Museum, Moscow
real_world.use: The original walking machine moves its feet on a near-straight path using Chebyshev's lambda linkage.
real_world.note: Uses the lambda form, a cognate of the Chebyshev linkage.

real_world.product: Chebyshev plantigrade (walking) machine, 1878
real_world.maker: P. L. Chebyshev; Polytechnic Museum, Moscow
real_world.use: Its legs use the lambda linkage, whose coupler point traces the same near-straight hoof path as the Hoekens linkage.
real_world.note: Closest real object: the lambda mechanism is a cognate of the Hoekens linkage, not a Hoekens linkage itself; no industrial Hoekens product found.

real_world.product: Reuleaux model S14, Roberts straight-line linkage (Dreieckslenker von Roberts), 1882
real_world.maker: Gustav Voigt Werkstatt; Cornell Reuleaux collection
real_world.use: Cast-iron and brass model showing the coupler point of the Roberts four-bar tracing an approximate straight line.

real_world.product: De Voglie underwater pile-sawing machine, c. 1756 to 1760
real_world.maker: De Voglie (published by Pierre Patte 1769; in Ferguson, Kinematics of Mechanisms)
real_world.use: A Roberts-type linkage guided a bar at the rear of the machine.
real_world.note: Historic machine; modern real uses are scarce.

real_world.product: Reuleaux model S15, inversion of Roberts linkage, 1882
real_world.maker: Gustav Voigt Werkstatt; Cornell Reuleaux collection
real_world.use: Model of the inverted Roberts triangle linkage.

real_world.product: Grasshopper engine from Clyde Wharf Works, c. 1840
real_world.use: Full-size half-beam grasshopper engine that powered the Clyde Wharf Works from 1840 to 1928.
real_world.note: Page does not name the linkage; grasshopper engines are the type that used it.

real_world.product: Oliver Evans Columbian engine, before 1813
real_world.maker: Oliver Evans (in Ferguson, Kinematics of Mechanisms)
real_world.use: The Evans linkage guided the piston rod and allowed a much lighter beam than Watt's motion.

real_world.product: Reuleaux model S5, four-bar straight-line mechanism after Evans, 1882
real_world.maker: Gustav Voigt Werkstatt; Cornell Reuleaux collection
real_world.use: Model of Evans' approximate straight-line four-bar.

real_world.product: Nissan Sentra SE-R Spec V (B15) rear beam axle
real_world.use: A Scott Russell linkage locates the twist-beam rear axle sideways.

real_world.product: Nissan Almera N16 and related Nissans (B14, N15, P11) rear axle
real_world.use: Factory Scott Russell lateral link on the rear beam, discussed with an adjustable aftermarket version.

real_world.product: Prim's blowing engine for House of Commons ventilation, 1877
real_world.maker: Mr. Prim, engineer to the Houses of Parliament (in Ferguson, Kinematics of Mechanisms)
real_world.use: A Peaucellier cell guided the crosshead of the steam-driven air pump and ran unusually quietly.

real_world.product: Peaucellier Inversor, Schilling series 24 model 10, c. 1900
real_world.use: Metal kinematic model in which the crank turns and one point traces an exact straight line.

real_world.product: Reuleaux model S35, Peaucellier straight-line mechanism, 1882
real_world.maker: Gustav Voigt Werkstatt; Cornell Reuleaux collection
real_world.use: Eight-link cast-iron and brass model giving exact straight-line motion.

real_world.product: Hart Inversor, Schilling series 24 model 11, c. 1900
real_world.use: Hourglass four-bar model in which one point moves in a circle and another in an exact straight line.
real_world.note: No real machine using Hart's inversor found; museum models are the closest real objects.

real_world.product: A. P. Rollett set of straight-line linkage models (accession 6636.3, Hart's inversor)
real_world.maker: A. P. Rollett; Whipple Museum, Cambridge
real_world.use: Wooden board model of Hart's inversor giving exact straight-line motion.
